rv.q: Her “Streetcar” is ferociously alive, all the way from from lights up to “I’ve always depended on the kindness of strangers.”
Overall, an impressively intense staging of a play that retains its power to shock, 70 years on.
Joanna Vanderham is stunning as Blanche.

Josh Seymour's production for the Crucible in Sheffield reminds us how endlessly compelling this tragedy of 'brutal desire' and self-delusion is, although it doesn't always yield performances powerful enough to motor it.
This production of A Streetcar Named Desire is just wonderful.
This Streetcar is certainly strong in many aspects, but stumbles over certain key points.

cn.t: Critics largely praise this revival's compelling performances and enduring relevance, though some find execution uneven. Patsy Ferran and Paul Mescal earn particular acclaim, while the Sheffield production draws more mixed notices.
